It drifts on ANY pub-boundary change, so any two campaigns that touch a pub boundary conflict there by construction. At the rate main is moving, a campaign can absorb to zero-behind and be stale again before it reaches the box -- which is exactly what happened to the-hallmark, twice.

WHY THE OBVIOUS FIX IS WRONG, so nobody proposes it in good faith. .gitattributes grants merge=union to three paths -- book/src/SUMMARY.md, book/src/frontier/idea-registry.md, docs/timings.md -- and all three are APPEND-ONLY LISTS where concatenating both sides is correct. The type-audit report is a rendered TABLE. Union would interleave two renderings silently. Its absence from that list is correct, not an oversight.

WHAT MIGHT ACTUALLY WORK, recorded for a human to rule on rather than done: a custom merge driver for declared generated paths that resolves by taking EITHER side, leaning on the chamber's `artifacts` phase to regenerate and commit the drift -- which it already does on every merge. The wrinkle is deployment: union is built into git, a custom driver needs `merge.<name>.driver` in each clone's config, so it would have to ride along with `make install-hooks`. And it would be silently wrong for a LOCAL merge that nobody regenerates after, which is the case scripts/hooks/post-merge already advises about and cannot enforce.

That is a change to merge semantics repo-wide. It is not an operator's call and I am not making it -- but five instances in one session with two campaigns blocked outright is the point at which it stops being anecdote.
